mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, notary, or competent company registry in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, in addition to notarization of the copy certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or official register of directors and legal representatives for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or corporate secretary of the corporate shareholder, certified by the competent registry where required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where the certificate is issued by a public authority; direct certified copy acceptable if issued by a licensed registered agent under national practice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the passport (biometric data page) of each individual shareholder, director and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the passport holder's country of residence or domicile

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address, being a bank statement or utility invoice issued within the preceding 90 days, for each individual UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated financial institution or utility company in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of Wealth and Source of Funds declaration, signed and dated by each individual UBO and principal shareholder, with supporting bank, tax or sale documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The declaring individual before a notary or a licensed fiduciary, with signature legalized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization of the notarial signature certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police Clearance / Certificate of Good Conduct issued within 90 days for each director and individual beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police authority or designated criminal record authority in the country of ordinary residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter issued by a regulated financial institution for each corporate shareholder and each individual beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The relevant regulated bank or financial institution where the shareholder or UBO maintains an account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; direct confidential bank-to-fiduciary transmission may be accepted where the Luxembourg licensed agent can verify provenance

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, legal representatives, directors, officers and authorized signatories against the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, US OFAC SDN and Consolidated Non-SDN lists, UK HM Treasury Consolidated Sanctions List, the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU Luxembourg) screening lists and any CSSF warning lists. Foreign and domestic PEP status, including immediate family members and close associates, must be identified and subjected to enhanced due diligence under Luxembourg AML Law articles 3 and 4. The appointed fiduciary must perform automated World-Check / Dow Jones / Refinitiv or equivalent screening, negative news review and source-of-wealth corroboration. Ongoing transaction and relationship monitoring is required for the duration of the business relationship and for five years thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online portal at lbr.lu, operating the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed names must be expressed using the Latin alphabet. The official languages for corporate purposes are Luxembourgish, French and German; English may be used where the name is not misleading and is otherwise lawful. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters and cannot be registered in native script. The legal form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'S.à r.l.' is mandatory for a SARL and may not be omitted, translated into arbitrary abbreviations, or placed in non-Latin script. The name must be distinctive, not contrary to public order or good morals, not misleading, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS-protected name or registered trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: OPCVM / SICAV / SICAF / OPCI / INVESTMENT COMPANY
CHAMBRE DE COMMERCE AND OTHER INSTITUTIONAL BODIES WITHOUT DUE AUTHORIZATION
HOLDING OR SUB-HOLDING ONLY WHEN SUCH USE WOULD IMPLY A REGULATED FINANCIAL HOLDING WITHOUT CSSF APPROVAL
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects a name, the applicant receives a reasoned refusal notice. Within five working days the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the RCS registrar, providing evidence of distinctiveness or a corrected name. If the refusal is confirmed, the applicant has eight calendar days from notification to lodge a formal appeal before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, commercial chamber) through a registered Luxembourg avocat. Concurrently, a new name may be submitted and reserved for a fresh 30-day window. An expiring reservation should be renewed before expiry if the notarial deed cannot be signed within the original 30-day period; renewal is subject to RCS administrative discretion.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted. Luxembourg law requires a SARL to have a registered office in the Grand Duchy but does not require the office to maintain physical operating assets. A licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent may provide the registered seat and letterbox facility. For an ISIC 6311 real-time video matching and social telephony business, a virtual office is acceptable at the incorporation stage and for RCS, tax and UBO filing purposes. However, to sustain Luxembourg corporate tax residence and economic substance, the strategic management functions such as board decisions, IT administration, contractual negotiations and risk oversight must be demonstrably exercised in Luxembourg. A pure virtual letterbox without substance gives rise to profit allocation, transfer-pricing and general anti-abuse rule exposure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk, estimated at 10-15% annual probability for a medium-risk digital services SARL where the registered office is a domiciliation address. Unannounced physical inspections are rare, with an estimated incidence below 5% per year, unless a criminal complaint, tax irregularity, or public order concern triggers direct inspection by the RCS, the police, or the Luxembourg direct tax administration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (consolidated 19 December 2020), Articles 710-1 et seq. (Société à Responsabilité Limitée, SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) and electronic publication; Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the professions of artisan, merchant and liberal professions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accessed electronically through the MyGuichet.lu / MyLBR e-filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (acte notarié de constitution) embodying the Articles of Association (statuts), filed with the RCS and published in the electronic compendium RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum share capital: EUR 12,000 (approx. USD 13,200), fully subscribed at formation. Each cash share must be paid in at least 20% at subscription (minimum EUR 2,400 effective paid-up); in-kind contributions must be fully freed within five years. The capital is blocked in a Luxembourg bank account opened in the name of the 'société en formation' until the notary executes the deed; no statutory escrow agent is mandated, but the notary requires the bank's blocked-funds certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED unanimously by the subscribers at the constitutive board meeting: 1. The draft articles of association of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) are adopted and approved. 2. The subscription of the entire share capital of EUR 12,000 is ratified; each cash share is subscribed in full, with 20% paid up at this time as prescribed by law. 3. The registered office is fixed at 12-14, avenue Monterey, L-2163 Luxembourg. 4. Mr./Ms. [Name] is appointed Manager (Gérant), acting individually, with full power of management and representation. 5. The Manager is instructed to file the deed for registration, publish the statutory statements, obtain establishment approval, and complete tax/social registrations. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and RCS Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS consultation desk via MyGuichet.lu / MyLBR portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run an ESE/RCS database search to verify the distinctiveness of the proposed corporate name against registered Luxembourg companies and relevant EEA trademarks. If clear, file the name reservation request electronically through MyGuichet and obtain the negative certificate (extrait de non-confusion) to be handed to the notary.
required_dossiers: Corporate name availability search application
Founders' identification documents
Short description of the corporate purpose (ISIC 6311 – real-time video matching and data hosting)
Power of attorney (if filed by an intermediary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where confusion or similarity is objected by the RCS, submit two alternative names accompanied by an explanatory memorandum and request reassessment within 8 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account and Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg licensed credit institution selected by the founders; notarial coordination
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name of the 'société en formation' (or of the founders on behalf of the company), deposit the subscribed cash capital of EUR 12,000 (minimum EUR 2,400 paid up), and obtain the notarial bank certificate (attestation de banque) confirming the blocking of funds until execution of the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Bank account application for a company-in-formation
AML/KYC forms and source-of-funds declaration
Passports/IDs and proof of residence of the subscribers
Draft statuts containing the corporate purpose and capital clauses
Corporate founders: certificate of good standing and board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of KYC queries, supply enhanced source-of-wealth documentation; the notary may accept funds held in a sworn escrow account if the bank delays, provided the bank certificate is dated within the legal validity window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Drafting and Execution of Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary in Luxembourg City – Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the French-language statuts with the notary: object clause covering real-time video matching and cross-border social telephony under ISIC 6311, registered office in Luxembourg, EUR 12,000 capital, SARL governance (gérants), fiscal year, and non-resident ownership provisions. Execute the deed before the notary, who verifies capital legality, obtains the bank certificate, and receives managers' declarations.
required_dossiers: Notarial draft statuts (certified by the notary)
Negative name certificate (extrait de non-confusion)
Bank certificate of capital blockage
Identity and address proof of subscribers and gérants
Subscribed share list (parts sociales register)
Signed plan financier (liquidity plan for the first 12 months)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary issues a deficiency list (requête) within 3 days; all documentation must be cured within 8 days, failing which the execution is postponed. No penalty is incurred if cured before the scheduled deed date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and RESA Publication (Legal Personality Perfection)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via MyGuichet.lu / MyLBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed authentic copy, statutory declarations of the gérants, and registered-office documents through the notary; pay the statutory RCS registration fee. The RCS enters the company in the register and arranges electronic publication in RESA, giving legal personality full effect vis-à-vis third parties.
required_dossiers: Authentic copy of the notarial incorporation deed
Managers' acceptance declarations and specimen signatures
Form C – corporate and legal representation data
Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of each gérant
Proof of registered office (lease deed or landlord's consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a rejection for insufficient documentation, resubmit the amended dossier within 15 days without losing priority; contested refusals may be appealed to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction des classes moyennes et des professions libérales; filed online via Guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within three months after RCS registration, file the establishment-permit application qualifying the company as a non-qualified commercial service provider (ISIC 6311), proving managers' good repute and identifying the business premises. The permit is delivered after verification of the criminal record and the physical address.
required_dossiers: Online application form (Form 12bis)
RCS extract issued within 3 months
Criminal record certificate of managers and persons in charge
Copy of lease or ownership title of the business premises
Identity documents of the legal representatives
Tax and social security compliance certificates (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If clarification is requested, file substantiating documents within 10 days; in case of refusal, administrative appeal lies to the Minister and thereafter to the Administrative Tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT and Social Security Registration (AEDT / CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) – via MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Luxembourg VAT number (numéro d'immatriculation TVA) to invoice cross-border video-match app services and app-store settlements; register simultaneously as employer with the CCSS to obtain the social insurance registration number for future payroll and workforce declarations.
required_dossiers: RCS extract after incorporation
VAT registration form (Formulaire 2)
Employer registration form (CCSS)
List of managers and their national IDs
Description of payment rails (Apple IAP, Paymentwall) for VAT characterization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For late filing, submit an explanatory request to the AEDT invoking force majeure or legitimate excuse; the administration may waive late-payment surcharges in justified cases, and CCSS deadlines may be regularized through a corrective declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Premises, Fire Safety and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commune of Luxembourg – Urban Planning and Building Department; Administration de la Prévention des Risques (APR); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the municipal occupancy certificate (certificat de conformité) for the office premises used as the registered office, complete the fire-safety review with the communal fire prevention service, and declare the workplaces to ITM; finalize structural and electrical conformity checks to permit occupation by the app's engineering, moderation, and customer-support teams.
required_dossiers: Office lease or deed of ownership with floor plan
Fire-safety compliance checklist approved by communal fire authorities
Electrical installation verification report (EN 50171 / NF C 15-100)
Structural load certificate for office floors (minimum 250 kg/m²)
ITM workplace declaration (EE1 form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the commune or APR rejects conformity, execute the listed remedial measures and schedule a re-inspection within 20 working days; if refusal persists, appeal the municipal decision to the communal board or tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction des classes moyennes et des professions libérales; environmental aspects under the Administration de l'Environnement (Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et de la Biodiversité)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement / Business Establishment Permit (non-qualified commercial sector – ISIC 6311) and, where applicable, environmental operating notification for non-classified IT premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement – Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et de la Biodiversité
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 4 – Non-classified activity (non classée): exempt from a full EIA report and prior integrated environmental permit, as the company operates software development and cloud-mediated video matching with no industrial production; a simple commencement notification (déclaration) to the Administration is sufficient for office premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Règlement grand-ducal of 24 November 2001 on urban wastewater treatment (COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L if sanitary water is discharged to municipal sewers); waste management under the Law of 21 March 2012 (European Waste Catalogue codes for WEEE, IT scrap, and packaging); no VOC-emitting manufacturing processes installed; any reserve emergency generator, if deployed, must meet stage V NRMM emission limits.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the communal fire prevention service (Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours); structural load inspection certificate for office floors (minimum 250 kg/m²); electrical installation verification per EN/IEC standards; occupational clearance by the ITM under the Luxembourg Labour Code, including workplace ergonomics and social premises inspection.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; unified electronic portal via Guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign investor establishing a Luxembourg SARL must first incorporate with the Luxembourg Business Register (RCSL) through a statutory corporate agent, obtaining the national matricule number. After incorporation, VAT registration is completed by filing Form A with the AEDT Bureau d'imposition TVA through MyGuichet.lu, disclosing the intended taxable activities, place of management, and estimated turnover. Non-resident non-established taxable persons may register directly with AEDT for a Luxembourg VAT identification number, subject to submission of proof of foreign corporate existence and identification of a fiscal representative within Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; an SARL is inherently a non-transparent company subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax. Available elective regimes include VAT group treatment under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, income tax fiscal unity under Article 164bis LIR for resident group companies, and the election to treat a civil partnership (SCSp) as transparent for tax purposes where appropriate construction is chosen. Hybrid mismatch elections are constrained by ATAD implementation and the Luxembourg anti-hybrid rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover for resident small-enterprise VAT exemption under Article 57 VAT Law; non-EU and non-established foreign suppliers have no general threshold and must register from the first taxable supply in Luxembourg unless covered by the EU One-Stop-Shop or reverse charge mechanism.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory digital stamping exists in Luxembourg. B2B e-invoicing is not generally mandatory, but electronic invoicing on the PEPPOL network (PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0) is required for supplies to Luxembourg public authorities. Tax invoices must comply with Articles 68 and 69 VAT Law; the VAT return and listing are filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu on a monthly, quarterly, or annual basis depending on taxable turnover.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union, provided the supplier obtains and retains conclusive documentary proof of export within statutory deadlines. Export-related services and services supplied to non-resident taxable persons may be outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under B2B place-of-supply rules; digital services to non-taxable customers outside the EU may also fall outside Luxembourg VAT. Goods exported from Luxembourg to EU Member States are taxable in the destination state rather than zero-rated in Luxembourg except where transitional distance-sale or OSS rules apply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Electronic Export System / ECS)
Bill of Lading, CMR, rail waybill, or air waybill evidencing physical movement
Proof of exit from the European Union endorsed by customs authorities
Commercial invoice and underlying supply contract
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement confirming receipt of payment from abroad
VAT registration certificate of the foreign purchaser where relevant
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT scrutinizes zero-rating claims and may retrospectively clawback VAT where export documentation is missing, incomplete, or not obtained within the 90-day documentary deadline, adding default interest calculated at the legal rate. Deliberate disguise or misuse of export zero-rating constitutes tax fraud and attracts administrative fines under Article 68 of the General Tax Law and criminal sanctions under the Luxembourg Criminal Code. False documentation may also trigger joint liability of any customs agent and a five-year clawback period in normal cases, extended to ten years in the event of proven fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) acts as the financial sector regulator, and Luxembourg maintains no separate foreign exchange administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full currency convertibility as a euro-area member state. Capital account and current account transactions are unrestricted under EU Treaty free movement of capital provisions. Profit remittances are free of exchange controls, subject only to standard corporate tax compliance, withholding tax clearances, and AML/KYC verification at the receiving bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline for export proceeds surrender and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts in EUR or any freely convertible currency may be retained in any bank account. No reporting obligation applies to the per-transaction level except under EU statistical balance-of-payments reporting thresholds administered by the BCL.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for EU-licensed or passporting electronic money institutions and payment institutions operating under a Luxembourg licence or valid EU passport. Low for offshore digital EMIs without CSSF licensing or EU passporting. Offshore EMIs cannot provide regulated payment services in Luxembourg; any such arrangement must be structured through a licensed local agent or sub-license, with full KYC/AML due diligence at the parent bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors of the SARL are normally required to attend an in-person onboarding interview at the chosen bank, or a recognised video-identification session supported by notarised, apostilled corporate documents and beneficial ownership declarations. Remote opening is materially more difficult for non-EU shareholders and requires a notarised power of attorney, legal entity identification numbers, and certified passport and proof-of-address documents. Enhanced due diligence will likely trigger a physical interview for ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-layer beneficial ownership and non-EU shareholder structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current official extract from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, notarised share register, full group organisational chart, passport copies, proof of residential address for each shareholder, director and ultimate beneficial owner, source-of-wealth statements, and independent legal confirmation of the chain of control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume microtransactions and anonymous user payments inherent to a random video match application
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed AML/KYC policy, transaction monitoring procedures, user identity verification (KYC) flow, payment processor due diligence file (Apple IAP, Paymentwall), business model documentation, expected transaction profile, customer risk assessment, and a written anti-money-laundering compliance manual approved by the directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital platform with minimal physical footprint and cross-border user base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Internal controls framework, sanctions screening and PEP screening procedure, FATF/TRA guidance adoption statement, independent compliance audit opinion, data residency and data protection impact assessment, and a risk-based customer acceptance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for initial capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised deed of contribution, bank reference letters from remitting banks, audited or independently reviewed financial statements of shareholders, source-of-funds documentation, and sworn declarations explaining the economic rationale and lawful origin of the injected capital.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are executed via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA credit transfer into the SARL's capital escrow account. The purpose code and free-text field 70 must clearly state 'equity contribution', 'capital increase', or 'shareholder loan' in compliance with the BCL statistical reporting and CSSF AML expectations. Supporting documents include the notarised resolution, shareholder list, updated incorporation documents, and proof of source of funds. Luxembourg banks may require a breakdown of foreign exchange rates if the injection is in a non-EUR currency.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements use SEPA credit transfers for EU counterparties, SWIFT MT103 for non-EU counterparties, and commercial letters of credit issued or confirmed by Luxembourg banks for documented trade transactions. All outbound payments are screened against EU and UN sanctions, and the SARL must retain underlying contracts, invoices, and customs or shipping documentation for audit trail purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Combined Interest Rate and Currency Swaps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts (balance sheet, income statement, notes and management report, where required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year-end (e.g., by 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered filing, administrative fines up to EUR 5,000, and potential administrative strike-off from the RCS upon persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (UBO declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each year, confirming data as at 31 December; any shareholding change must be updated within one month of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines and imprisonment for responsible managers under the Luxembourg UBO Law of 13 January 2019; enforcement measures by the RBE and the Public Prosecutor, including corrective orders and financial penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (IRC) and net wealth tax return (IF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 December of the year following the financial year-end, subject to published ACD extension calendars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Ex officio assessment, late-payment interest at 0.8% per month on unpaid tax, administrative fines under the General Tax Law, and criminal sanctions for willful omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of shareholders approving annual accounts and granting discharge to management
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company statutory records (shareholders' minutes book); no public filing to RCS unless a publication requirement applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Management civil liability for failure to convene; judicial convocation upon shareholder petition at company cost; potential judicial compulsory winding-up in serious default cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint a certified independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) when it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average workforce above 50 employees. Mandatory audit also applies to SARLs with 25 or more shareholders, financial-sector undertakings, and certain public-interest entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, and the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial accounting and annual accounts); IFRS as endorsed by the EU may be applied voluntarily and is mandatory for listed entities and credit institutions where applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every Luxembourg SARL must confirm its central UBO file in the RBE at least once per calendar year, regardless of whether a change occurred. Any transfer of shares or qualifying ownership change must be reported within one month of completion; after any update or confirmation, the entity remains subject to the following year's annual confirmation cycle.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $500 – $3,000 per year (registered agent and registered address services in Luxembourg City, depending on provider and compliance scope)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $7,000 – $25,000 per year (certified audit for a low-to-medium risk digital and video-matching SARL, depending on turnover and year-end complexity)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.80% aggregate headline rate for Luxembourg City (CIT 15% + solidarity/unemployment surcharge 7% of CIT = 1.05% + municipal business tax 6.75%; municipal business tax varies by commune, is deductible for CIT, so the effective combined burden is slightly below the headline; rate applicable to FY beginning 1 January 2025).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption of qualifying dividends and capital gains on shareholdings equal to or above 10% of the target's share capital or acquired for at least EUR 1.2m, held at least 12 months, with subject-to-tax condition. IP regime: 80% exemption of net qualifying intellectual-property income (copyrighted software/patents, nexus ratio applies), producing an effective ~5% rate on IP income. Notional interest deduction (NID) of 4% per annum on the increase in (cash) equity. Net wealth tax at 0.5%, with minimum net wealth tax of EUR 535/EUR 3,210 based on fixed financial assets. No economic substance exemption; the video-match app's software IP held by the SARL can benefit from the IP box only with genuine local substance.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_rule: Unlimited carry-forward of net operating losses; no carry-back permitted. Loss schedules must be annexed to the Form 520 and substantiated to preserve the attribute.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 520 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, l'impôt commercial communal et l'impôt sur la fortune) filed electronically through the MyGuichet.lu eCDF portal of the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); non-resident taxpayers must appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative (mandataire fiscal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 30 June of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end (fiscal year = calendar year for the SARL unless otherwise authorized); extension to 30 September is generally granted for e-filing, and to 31 December where a registered approved tax advisor (fiduciaire/cabinet d'avocats) files the return. Quarterly prepayments of CIT/municipal business tax fall due on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December of the fiscal year; the remaining balance follows the final tax assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the assessment year, fiscal year commencement and closing dates, legal form (SARL), RCSL registration number, tax file number, and status of the declaration (original/amendment).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL/shareholder: declare only Luxembourg-source items (PE profits, Luxembourg-situs real property, and, where applicable, Luxembourg-source IP income) unless treaty benefits or a permanent establishment filing election apply; attach TRC-based residence statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, registered office address, principal activity (ISIC 6311 / NAICS 519130 video-chat platform), director and manager names, share capital, shareholder registry data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Luxembourg registered agent details and the appointed fiscal representative; RBE/UBO references for the SARL's ultimate beneficial owners must match the Luxembourg register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from the video-match app (Apple IAP and Paymentwall net revenue), COGS, cloud/hosting costs, staff costs, intercompany service fees, depreciation (including IP amortization), and reconciliation of commercial result to fiscal result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border intercompany flows (payment-processing commissions, user-acquisition spend, content-moderation fees) must be supported by OECD-compliant TP documentation; attach the Local File where applicable thresholds are exceeded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C - IP, Royalties and Financial Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Royalty/licence income from the matching algorithm and software, dividends, interest and other financial products; IP-box (80% exemption) computation with nexus ratio; participation exemption schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident licensors: disclose any Luxembourg-source royalties and claim treaty relief; to the extent resident in a DTA state, Luxembourg does not levy domestic WHT on outbound royalties, but the income is disclosed for exchange-of-information and CFC purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D - Deductions, Loss Carry-Forward and NID
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating deductions, exceptional charges, loss carry-forward utilization (unlimited), notional interest deduction computation, and municipal business tax base adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses incurred in the Luxembourg branch/PE are credited only against Luxembourg-source income; the NID applies proportionally to the PE's net equity where a non-resident company maintains a PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section E - Net Wealth Tax Base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unitary net wealth tax return integrated into Form 520 (0.5% of net wealth), minimum NWT determination (EUR 535/EUR 3,210), participation-exempt shareholdings deducted from the tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not subject to Luxembourg net wealth tax on shares; the PE's wealth allocable to Luxembourg is reported with a PE Annex and any treaty apportionment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section F - Withholding Taxes, Credits and Assessments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of dividend/constructive-dividend WHT (15%), WHT credits, foreign tax credits, prepayments made, and resulting balance due or receivable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parents: attach the Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption form/treaty rate certificate and TRC to avoid a 15% WHT or to obtain a Form 105 refund of over-withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: coercive fine (Zwangsmittel/Ordnungsstrafe) up to EUR 2,500 per tax under Section 412 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung); the ACD may issue a formal reminder and, on continued default, assess estimated tax (which becomes due with 0.6% monthly late-payment interest). Failure to pay assessed balances: interest at 0.6% per month (7.2% p.a.) on the overdue principal. Incorrect or grossly negligent declarations: additional tax of up to 50% of the under-declared tax; intentional evasion: additional tax up to 100% plus criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% final Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends paid by an SARL; reduced to 0% for qualifying distributions to EU/EEA parent companies under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (10% participation) and under certain DTAs; treaty rates generally 5% (10%+ capital/quota) or 15% (portfolio) where the recipient is a beneficial owner in a DTA state.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from the reduced or exempt rate, the shareholder provides the Luxembourg paying entity before the distribution with: (i) a tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the DTA-state tax authority for the relevant calendar year; (ii) a declaration of beneficial ownership and of the shareholding period; and (iii) where applicable, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive participation statement. The paying entity files the withholding exemption/deduction documentation with the ACD; if the 15% WHT has been withheld, the shareholder recovers the excess through a Form 105 refund application within the statutory deadlines, supported by the TRC and an audited computation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: no domestic withholding tax on royalties and no domestic withholding tax on interest paid by a Luxembourg company (Luxembourg fully implements the EU Interest & Royalties Directive for associated enterprises). Treaty: source-state WHT reserved rates (commonly 10%-15% on interest, 5%-10% on royalties) are not exercised by Luxembourg as the payer's jurisdiction, so no WHT is deducted on outbound IP licensing fees or intra-group loan interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR. Local File (Form/annex records) must be prepared and filed with the tax declaration where intragroup transactions exceed the following thresholds per fiscal year: goods EUR 5,000,000; services EUR 1,000,000; financial transactions (loans, interest, guarantees) EUR 250,000; IP/royalty transactions EUR 250,000. Master File required where the multinational group's consolidated revenue is at least EUR 50,000,000; Luxembourg CbC reporting obligations mirror EU Directive 2016/881/EU for groups above EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no ESR law of the UAE/offshore type, but powerful substance-based anti-abuse doctrines apply: (1) EU ATAD GAAR (Art. 6) and the 2019 tax-amnesty/circular practice recharacterize artificial arrangements lacking commercial justification; (2) treaty-benefit and participation-exemption claims require economic substance (local management, employees, decision-making, and bank accounts in Luxembourg); (3) the pending EU Unshell Directive (ATAD 3) indicators scrutinize 'letterbox' SARLs with passive income, nominee directors and no local premises; (4) for the video-match app, the ACD expects genuine content-moderation, sales, IP-administration and treasury functions to be performed in Luxembourg to support IP-box and PE-protective outcomes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission of Apple IAP/Paymentwall revenues, fabricated intercompany invoices, hidden UK/Latvian/Cyprus marketing fees, or non-reporting of the SARL's software IP migration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the full tax at the 22.80% combined rate; additional tax up to 100% of the evaded tax; 0.6% monthly late-payment interest; criminal fines (Criminal Code and Section 395 AO) of up to EUR 250,000 plus imprisonment of up to 5 years for controllers; confiscation of criminal proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/managers who signed the false declaration are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and fines; Luxembourg criminal procedure permits travel bans (interdiction judiciaire de sortie du territoire) and provisional custody pending trial; a conviction automatically disqualifies the individual from managing a Luxembourg commercial company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying non-arm's-length acquisition fees, management fees or royalty remittances to related parties in low-tax jurisdictions; failing to prepare the Local File; intragroup migration of the app's algorithm IP at below-market value without an exit-tax and TP study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary TP adjustment restoring arm's-length income; secondary adjustment (imputed dividend or loan) with 15% WHT exposure; 0.6% monthly interest; negligence surcharge of up to 50% of the additional assessment; criminal escalation where the TP file is falsified.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers approving the pricing are personally liable vis-à-vis the SARL for damages under company-law standards (faute de gestion) and face criminal liability if the documentation is knowingly fraudulent; ACD officials may refer the file to the State Prosecutor (Parquet).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Letterbox Abuse (Lack of Substance)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SARL with no premises, no employees, no operating bank account, nominee management resident abroad, all board decisions taken outside Luxembourg, and systematic pass-through of profits to offshore group entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR recharacterization of the SARL as a sham, denial of treaty benefits and of the participation exemption/IP-box, disallowance of deductible payments (with reclassification as constructive dividends subject to 15% WHT), retroactive reassessment, and administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 for procedural non-compliance; possible compulsory strike-off from the RCSL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and de facto directors are jointly liable for taxes re-assessed due to the arrangement; criminal sanctions follow if the shell was used to commit fraud; directors may be ordered by the commercial court to pay the company's tax liabilities as civil damages and may be subject to exit visits/restrictions while under investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register the ultimate beneficial owners in Luxembourg's RBE register; unreported high-volume IAP cash flows; absence of KYC and AML/CTF program despite the 'Medium_Risk_Enhanced' banking risk tier; income routed through Paymentwall to sanctioned parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the AML Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) up to EUR 250,000 for legal persons; RBE registration failure penalized at EUR 125-EUR 250,000 per infraction; criminal sanctions for money laundering (Criminal Code Art. 506-1 et seq.) with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines for legal persons up to EUR 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the designated compliance officer may be criminally prosecuted where willful blindness to suspicious flows is established; Luxembourg courts have imposed personal fines, seizure of assets, travel bans and disqualification orders against non-compliant managers; directors remain liable for the SARL's AML fines unless they prove delegation to a suitable and independent compliance function.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and Constructive Dividend Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits or granting shareholder benefits (loans on non-market terms, shareholder use of the app's IT infrastructure, excessive monopoly royalties) without withholding 15%; failing to account for WHT on liquidation dividends or on profit participations to corporate shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SARL as the withholding agent is liable for the full un-withheld 15% WHT, plus 0.6% monthly interest and a withholding penalty of up to 10% of the amount; the recipient shareholder's treaty/PSD claim is lost if the statutory formalities were not met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The manager who caused the distribution without WHT filing is personally liable to the Treasury for the un-collected WHT (recourse of the company's liability); prosecution is possible for fraudulent reduction of movable assets subject to WHT; disqualification from office follows an unsatisfied tax liability declaration.
